articles.title: Michael Jordan’s legacy keeps growing 23 years after retirement as his sneaker empire reaches No. 41
articles.standfirst: The No. 23 walked off an NBA court for the final time in 2003, but the story attached to his name never really stopped moving
articles.summary: The No. 23 walked off an NBA court for the final time in 2003, but the story attached to his name never really stopped moving
articles.body:
F or Michael Jordan, numbers have always meant something. Six championships. Five MVP awards. Ten scoring titles. And, above all of them, 23 the number that became so inseparable from the man that generations of kids wanted it on their backs simply because he had worn it first.

On April 16, 2003, Jordan walked onto an NBA court for the final time. He was 40 years old, wearing a Washington Wizards uniform instead of Chicago red, when Philadelphia intentionally fouled him late in the game so he could score the final two points of his career from the free-throw line. The crowd rose for him, and eventually Jordan disappeared toward the locker room. Basketball's No. 23 was finally done.

Twenty-three years later a coincidence almost too perfect for Michael Jordan another number has arrived. Jordan Brand has officially unveiled the Air Jordan 41 , the 41st chapter of a sneaker story that began when Jordan was a 21-year-old rookie and Nike took an enormous gamble on a young guard from North Carolina.

The 41 doesn't represent Jordan's age, championships or another jersey number. It is simply the 41st numbered Air Jordan. Yet reaching it says something remarkable: the shoes kept going long after the player stopped.

It started with a shoe that wasn't supposed to become this

Before there could be an Air Jordan 41, there had to be an Air Jordan 1.

Jordan's relationship with Nike began during his rookie season in 1984, and the first Air Jordan arrived commercially in 1985 . The black-and-red story surrounding those early shoes became sneaker mythology: the NBA objected to footwear that violated its uniform rules, and Nike transformed that controversy into marketing gold.

The famous tale that Jordan was fined $5,000 every time he wore the AJ1 in an NBA game isn't quite accurate. Nike itself now acknowledges that the shoe at the center of the original dispute was a black-and-red Nike Air Ship worn in the 1984 preseason. But the legend helped make the Air Jordan feel rebellious before sneaker culture even had a name.

And then something much bigger happened. People didn't only want to watch Michael Jordan. They wanted to wear Michael Jordan.

The Air Jordan 3 arrived in 1988 with Tinker Hatfield's design, elephant print and the Jumpman imagery that would eventually become recognizable far beyond basketball. The Air Jordan 4 became attached forever to “The Shot” over Craig Ehlo in the 1989 playoffs.

The Air Jordan 11 became one of the defining shoes of Jordan's return from baseball and later gained another life through Space Jam. The black-and-red Air Jordan 12 became inseparable from the legendary 1997 “Flu Game.” And the Air Jordan 13 accompanied Jordan into the final championship run of The Last Dance .

Some Jordans have become more valuable than houses

Perhaps the strangest proof of what Jordan created is what people are now willing to pay for shoes he actually wore.

A pair of Air Jordan 13s worn by Jordan during Game 2 of the 1998 NBA Finals sold for $2.2 million in 2023. Then came something even more extraordinary: the “Dynasty Collection,” consisting of six individual sneakers Jordan wore in the championship-clinching games of all six Bulls title runs. The collection sold for $8 million in 2024. They weren't even six complete pairs. They were six individual shoes.

There have been even stranger relics. A pair of Air Jordan 1s connected to a 1985 exhibition in Italy was sold with a piece of shattered backboard glass reportedly still embedded in the sole, a souvenir from the night Jordan dunked hard enough to break the glass.

Another pair associated with the game in which he fractured his left foot in 1985 sold for more than $400,000. Shoes once designed to be destroyed on a basketball court eventually became artifacts people handle like paintings.

That transformation has made Jordan extraordinarily wealthy, but the size of the business is perhaps more impressive than any estimate of his personal royalties. Nike reported $7.034 billion in Jordan Brand revenue during fiscal 2026 alone.

Forty years after the first Air Jordan, this is no nostalgic side business surviving on old photographs. It remains a multibillion-dollar global brand.

At 63, Michael Jordan is still influencing the shoe

That may be the most surprising part of the Air Jordan 41.

Jordan isn't merely an old photograph used to sell it. At 63, he was among the athletes whose feedback informed its development . Jordan Brand describes the AJ41 as lighter and more responsive, built around a first-of-its-kind 3D nano mesh upper, full-length ZoomX foam, Zoom Strobel cushioning and additional Air Zoom. The first colorways are inspired by gemstones, with each intended to represent qualities such as strength, courage, passion and creativity.

The first version is appropriately called “Ruby.” It arrives dressed in the red that has followed Jordan through so much of his life, and Nike has priced it at $205. Look closely and there is even another tiny reminder of the man behind it: the official color description includes “Infrared 23.” Forty-one shoes later, 23 is still there.

And Jordan himself hasn't exactly disappeared. He co-owns 23XI Racing even the NASCAR team's name combines his 23 with Denny Hamlin's 11 and just days before the AJ41 unveiling, Jordan visited the team's Airspeed headquarters to speak with its drivers and personnel ahead of NASCAR's postseason.

Meanwhile, another chapter of his brief return to NBA television appears to be closing: a report on August 27 said Jordan is not expected to return to NBC's NBA coverage after one season as a special contributor. Even at 63, his relationship with competition seems difficult to completely leave behind.

Maybe that's why the Air Jordan 41 feels different when viewed through the entire story.

A young Michael Jordan once put on the first shoes carrying his name without knowing whether there would ever be a second pair, much less a 41st model. He played his final NBA game on April 16, 2003, and left the floor with 32,292 career points, six rings and a number 23 already immortal.

Now, 23 years later, the player is long retired, but the footsteps haven't stopped.

Michael Jordan wore No. 23. His shoes have now reached No. 41. And somewhere between those two numbers lies one of the rarest achievements in sports: a career that ended, and a legacy that simply refused to.

articles.title: Kevin Durant’s AI jackpot may be the greatest athlete investment ever
articles.standfirst: The return could exceed what Durant is earning this season as an NBA player
articles.summary: The return could exceed what Durant is earning this season as an NBA player
articles.body:
K evin Durant has spent nearly two decades making defenders look helpless on the basketball court. But his latest victory may be even more impressive than anything he has accomplished in the NBA.

According to i nvestor and entrepreneur Joe Pompliano, Durant's early investment in artificial intelligence company Hugging Face has reportedly turned a combined $250,000 investment into a payout exceeding $60 million following Nvidia's acquisition of the company for $12.9 billion.

If the estimates are accurate, the transaction would rank among the most successful investments ever made by a professional athlete.

And perhaps most remarkably, the return could exceed what Durant is earning this season as an NBA player.

A massive return on a small initial bet

Pompliano revealed on social media that Durant and longtime business partner Rich Kleiman participated in Hugging Face's seed and Series A fundraising rounds through their investment platform, 35V. According to Pompliano, Durant invested $100,000 during the company's seed round and another $150,000 during its Series A financing.

Years later, that relatively modest $250,000 commitment appears to have generated a return worth more than $60 million. "Kevin Durant and his business partner, Rich Kleiman, invested in Hugging Face's seed & Series A fundraising rounds," Pompliano wrote. "And it just happens that tech giant Nvidia just acquired the company for $12.9 billion."

He added that the investment likely generated a profit that surpassed Durant's on-court earnings for the current season. For most investors, a return of that magnitude would represent a once-in-a-lifetime outcome. For Durant, it is another example of how aggressively he has approached business opportunities away from basketball..

More than an NBA superstar

Durant remains one of the highest-paid athletes in the world. The future Hall of Famer is currently playing under a two-year, $90 million contract extension and is set to earn nearly $44 million during the 2026-27 campaign. Combined with his lifetime Nike agreement and previous contracts, Durant has already surpassed $500 million in career NBA earnings.

Unlike many athletes who rely primarily on endorsement deals, Durant has increasingly positioned himself as a venture capitalist. Alongside Kleiman, he has built 35V into one of the most active athlete-led investment firms in sports.

The company has invested across technology, media, sports, and consumer brands, focusing on early-stage opportunities with significant growth potential. The Hugging Face investment appears to be one of the firm's biggest successes to date.

articles.title: The heartbreaking situation that Kobe Bryant's sister goes through every year on her daughter's birthday
articles.standfirst: Shaya Bryant reveals why her daughter’s birthday is also one of the hardest days of the year
articles.summary: Shaya Bryant reveals why her daughter’s birthday is also one of the hardest days of the year
articles.body:
August 23 is a date filled with emotions that are difficult to separate in Shaya Bryant’s world. It’s the birthday of her daughter, Autumn , but it’s also the birthday of her younger brother, Kobe Bryant.

Since Kobe’s death in 2020, what should be a joyful family occasion has also become a painful annual reminder of the NBA legend she lost.

Shaya recently opened up about the complicated emotions surrounding the date while appearing on the Born To The Game podcast. She described August 23 as both “a beauty and a curse,” explaining how public celebrations of Kobe’s life can bring comfort while also reopening the wounds of grief.

Kobe was born on August 23, 1978, and Autumn was born on the same date in 2008. The coincidence was especially remarkable because Kobe had apparently predicted that his niece would arrive on his birthday.

Shaya recalled that Autumn was due on August 21, but Kobe told her that he believed the baby would come two days later.

“She was due August 21st. And when I was pregnant, he was like, ‘Oh, no. She’s coming on my birthday.’ I was like, ‘There ain’t no way.’ ‘Cause that means she’s two days late and she’s getting evicted,” said Shaya .

“There’s no way. And sure as… she came when he was playing in the Olympics in 2008. So while he was playing, I was pushing. Literally. So she was born same birthday.”

Today, that shared birthday has taken on an entirely different meaning for the Bryant family.

Kobe and his 13-year-old daughter, Gianna , were among nine people who died in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California, on January 26, 2020. The tragedy continues to cast a shadow over significant dates connected to Kobe , particularly his birthday.

The painful reality behind August 23

Shaya explained that grief doesn’t necessarily disappear with time. Instead, important dates can bring those feelings back to the surface.

“It’s just so weird… like I said, when people pass, like our grandparents when they’re older, but with this situation or this happening, it’s more of, it’s like a band-aid, right?” Shaya stated.

“So you think you’re healing and the wound has closed, but then there are anniversaries that come up, birthdays that come up, different things. And it’s such in a public manner that it’s everywhere, like you can’t really heal… nor escape it.”

Kobe’s global fame makes that process even harder. Every August, social media fills with photographs, career highlights, tributes and memories celebrating his life and accomplishments.

While Shaya appreciates the love shown to her brother, she also can’t simply escape the reminders.

She admitted that balancing the two emotions is difficult because she wants her daughter to enjoy her birthday while she’s also grieving and remembering her brother.

The timing is particularly significant because August 24 is recognized as Kobe Bryant Day in Los Angeles and Orange County. The date reflects the two jersey numbers he wore during his 20-season career with the Los Angeles Lakers, No. 8 and No. 24.

Kobe spent his entire NBA career with the Lakers, winning five championships and earning 18 All-Star selections. The franchise retired both of his numbers in 2017, making him the first player in Lakers history to have two numbers retired.

articles.title: LeBron James and Savannah James spend time with children in Akron ahead of his debut with the 76ers
articles.standfirst: James’ latest community effort highlights a legacy that goes far beyond basketball
articles.summary: James’ latest community effort highlights a legacy that goes far beyond basketball
articles.body:
LeBron James may be preparing for the next chapter of his extraordinary NBA career, but his connection to Akron remains as strong as ever.

As the basketball icon gets ready for the new season with the Philadelphia 76ers, he continues to make an impact in the community that has been central to his life and legacy.

James ’ commitment to his hometown was highlighted again as the LeBron James Family Foundation celebrated the ninth anniversary of the I PROMISE School in Akron.

The milestone offered another reminder that, despite his demanding basketball career, James hasn’t lost sight of the young people and families who call his hometown home.

The foundation marked the occasion by sharing images of students returning to school while reflecting on the organization’s journey.

Over the past nine years, the I PROMISE School has grown into more than an educational institution, with its programs designed to support students academically while also helping their families and strengthening the wider Akron community.

The foundation emphasized that its original promise to stand behind students remains unchanged, even as the school and its surrounding programs have evolved.

LeBron’s Akron legacy continues beyond basketball

The I PROMISE School has expanded its approach over the years, incorporating athletics, family support and community-building initiatives alongside education.

Its House system and I PROMISE Athletics program are among the efforts aimed at encouraging accountability, friendship, personal growth and teamwork.

That work represents a particularly personal part of James ’ legacy. Akron is where he grew up and developed into one of basketball’s biggest stars, and he’s repeatedly used his platform to create opportunities for children in the area.

His latest involvement comes at an interesting moment in his career. James stunned basketball fans in July when he revealed that he’d decided to continue playing after initially believing his previous season could have been his last.

He ultimately chose to sign with the 76ers for his record-breaking 24th NBA season.

James explained that his decision wasn’t motivated by money or outside pressure. Instead, he said he still loves basketball, wants to compete and believes he can help Philadelphia challenge for a championship.

While his attention will soon shift toward preparing for his debut with the 76ers, his recent activity in Akron shows that his priorities extend well beyond the court.

The timing has also been a memorable one for James and his family. His wife, Savannah James , recently celebrated her 40th birthday on Aug. 27.

LeBron marked the occasion with a heartfelt social media tribute, calling Savannah his “queen” and expressing his love and appreciation for her.

As James begins another chapter in Philadelphia, his connection to Akron isn’t going anywhere. His playing career may eventually come to an end, but the work he and his family have invested in the city could remain one of the most enduring parts of his legacy.

articles.summary: The Warriors are ready to give Curry everything he needs to finish his career at home
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors appear ready to give Stephen Curry something almost every superstar wants at the end of a legendary career: complete control over his future.

Curry becomes eligible for a new extension on August 29, with the maximum deal reportedly worth two years and approximately $136.7 million.

If he accepts it, the agreement would keep him in Golden State through the 2028-29 season and take his total earnings over the next three years to more than $199 million, including his roughly $62.6 million salary for 2026-27.

That could mean taking the maximum, accepting less money to give the franchise greater roster flexibility, or waiting until next summer to become an unrestricted free agent.

The message is clear, as the Warriors don't want to dictate how Curry's final chapter should look.

Keeping Curry is also a complicated basketball decision for Golden State. The 38-year-old remains one of the league's most influential players, but his age and recent injury history make a long-term commitment more complicated than it would've been earlier in his career.

Curry appeared in only 43 games last season after dealing with a knee injury that kept him sidelined for roughly two months. Even so, his importance to the Warriors extends far beyond what he produces on the court.

He has delivered four NBA championships, changed the way basketball is played and become the defining face of the Golden State franchise.

His presence also remains enormously valuable commercially, making the decision to keep him in the Bay Area about much more than salary-cap calculations.

A maximum extension would guarantee Curry's place in Golden State through the latter stages of his career, but it could also make it harder for the Warriors to add another superstar.

The organization has explored major opportunities involving players such as Giannis Antetokounmpo, LeBron James and Jaylen Brown , yet none of those blockbuster moves came to fruition.

That leaves Golden State facing a difficult balancing act. The Warriors want to maximize whatever remains of Curry's championship window while also ensuring they're not left without a path forward once their franchise icon eventually retires.

Still, everything currently points toward Curry finishing his career where it began. General manager Mike Dunleavy has indicated that neither the team nor Curry is considering another destination, while the Warriors reportedly have no intention of trading him.

After everything Curry has given the franchise, Golden State appears prepared to let its greatest player determine how his final chapter should unfold.

articles.title: Shaquille O’Neal’s latest skill? NBA legend is learning Spanish faster than expected
articles.standfirst: The legendary center's post-playing career has been defined by versatility
articles.summary: The legendary center's post-playing career has been defined by versatility
articles.body:
Shaquille O’Neal has built a career out of surprising people. The four-time NBA champion dominated opposing centers during his Hall of Fame basketball career. After retirement, he successfully transitioned into broadcasting, business, entertainment, music, and philanthropy. Few athletes have managed to remain as visible and influential after leaving the court as the larger-than-life superstar known simply as "Shaq."

Now, according to a young professional basketball player from Colombia, O’Neal may be adding another talent to his ever-growing list: speaking Spanish. Michael Martinez, a professional player for Toros del Valle in Colombia and a rising social media personality known as Colombian College Hooper, recently spent time with the NBA legend and came away impressed by O’Neal’s ability to pick up a new language.

A meeting between two basketball worlds

Martinez has built a following by documenting his journey through basketball, sharing the realities of playing professionally overseas with fans from around the globe. Through social media, he has provided a behind-the-scenes look at life as an international player while inspiring young athletes who dream of pursuing basketball beyond the traditional pathways in the United States.

His recent interaction with O’Neal offered followers a glimpse into a different side of the NBA icon. According to Martinez , one of the most surprising takeaways from their time together was how quickly O’Neal seemed to grasp Spanish words and phrases.

It's easy to forget that O’Neal has always been known for more than basketball. Throughout his career, he has demonstrated an unusual curiosity and willingness to explore new interests, whether that meant becoming a recording artist, earning advanced academic degrees, launching successful business ventures, or working as a television analyst.

Shaq's reputation for reinvention

O’Neal's post-playing career has been defined by versatility. While many former athletes remain connected exclusively to their sport, Shaq has consistently expanded his horizons. He has served as a television personality, entrepreneur, DJ, investor, law enforcement supporter, and motivational speaker, among many other roles.

That willingness to embrace new challenges has helped him remain one of the most recognizable sports figures in the world. The prospect of becoming conversational, or even fluent, in Spanish would only broaden his ability to connect with fans internationally.

Basketball's popularity throughout Latin America continues to grow, and O’Neal already enjoys a massive following in countries across the region. Developing Spanish-language skills could create even more opportunities for engagement with those audiences.

articles.title: Stephen Curry arrived at Warriors alone and built his most important team over 17 seasons while becoming an NBA legend
articles.standfirst: At 38, Curry is facing another enormous decision after spending nearly half his life building something much bigger than anyone could have imagined in 2009
articles.summary: At 38, Curry is facing another enormous decision after spending nearly half his life building something much bigger than anyone could have imagined in 2009
articles.body:
S tephen Curry was 21 years old when the Golden State Warriors called his name with the seventh pick of the 2009 NBA Draft. He arrived without a championship, without an MVP award and without any idea that the franchise taking a chance on him would eventually become almost impossible to separate from his name. He wasn't married yet, either.

Seventeen seasons later, Curry has given Golden State four NBA championships, won two MVP awards and become the greatest three-point shooter the league has ever seen. The skinny guard from Davidson became the face of a dynasty and one of the most recognizable athletes in the world. Now, at 38, the Warriors can put another extraordinary number in front of him: a two-year extension worth as much as $136.7 million.

But that only tells half of what Curry built during those 17 seasons

In 2011, two years after the Warriors drafted him, Curry married Ayesha, the girl he had first met as a teenager. A year later, Riley was born. Curry was still three years away from winning his first NBA championship, and the little girl who would eventually steal the show at his press conferences arrived before the basketball world fully understood what her father was about to become.

Then Curry's two teams started growing almost side by side. Ryan was born in July 2015 , just weeks after Curry won his first NBA championship. Canon arrived in 2018, right in the middle of the Warriors dynasty, after Golden State had won its third championship in four seasons. And in May 2024, Caius arrived. By then, Curry had four rings, two MVP awards, a Finals MVP and virtually nothing left to prove on a basketball court.

Golden State made Curry the face of a franchise. At home, he is simply one of six

Riley is 14 now. Ryan is 11. Canon is 8. Caius, the only one who will grow up without remembering the beginning of his father's extraordinary run, is 2. Stephen and Ayesha celebrated their 15th wedding anniversary this summer.

Those ages matter because they show just how much life has happened while Curry was busy making basketball history.

The 21-year-old who arrived at Golden State in 2009 is now a husband and father of four. He has watched his oldest daughter go from sitting on his lap at press conferences to becoming a teenager. His children have watched him win championships, break records, suffer injuries, come home from road trips and get up to do it all over again.

And Curry doesn't talk about that part of his life as something secondary to basketball. Earlier this year, he called raising four children with Ayesha “beautiful chaos.” Watching four different personalities develop, he said, has been the “best gift and responsibility” of their lives.

The Warriors can offer Curry $136.7 million and the possibility of playing through age 40. For Golden State, the decision could shape the final years of the greatest player in franchise history. For Curry, those same years will also happen while Riley becomes a young woman, Ryan moves deeper into her teenage years, Canon continues growing up and little Caius begins forming the childhood memories he may one day have of his father still playing in the NBA.

None of that means Curry is ready to walk away. Basketball remains part of who he is, and he has spoken about the court still being his happy place. But at 38, time looks different than it did at 21.

When Curry arrived in 2009, Golden State gave him a jersey and a place to begin his NBA career. Over the next 17 seasons, he helped turn that team into a dynasty.

Away from the arena, he and Ayesha were building another one.

And now, as one team decides how much it is willing to give Stephen Curry for the next two years, the other one is already waiting for him at home.

articles.title: Ja Morant returns to his old high school with daughter in his arms to see permanent tribute inside gym
articles.summary: Ja Morant returned to the place where his basketball journey began, and this time he wasn't alone.
articles.body:
Ja Morant returned to the place where his basketball journey began, and this time he wasn't alone.

The NBA star walked into Crestwood High School in Sumter, South Carolina, smiling and greeting people with his 7-year-old daughter Kaari in his arms as the school unveiled a permanent insignia inside the gym honoring his journey from Sumter to the NBA.

It's a very different scene from Morant's days as a teenager walking through the same school. He left Crestwood as its all-time leading scorer with 1,679 points before eventually becoming an NBA superstar.

The homecoming also gave something back to the next generation. Nike and Hibbett awarded $50,000 to Crestwood's boys and girls basketball programs as Morant returned to the gym where his own story started.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama’s summer transformation has NBA fans convinced a revenge tour is coming
articles.standfirst: The Spurs franchise cornerstone spent the offseason focused on adding strength
articles.summary: The Spurs franchise cornerstone spent the offseason focused on adding strength
articles.body:
V ictor Wembanyama was already one of the most terrifying players in basketball. Now, according to a growing number of fans on social media, he might be even bigger.

Photos and videos of the San Antonio Spurs superstar during France's recent international games have sent the basketball world into a frenzy, with many observers convinced that Wemby added significant muscle over the summer.

Some fans have even speculated that the 22-year-old may have grown taller, with reports and online discussions suggesting the French phenom could now stand around 7-foot-6 or taller. One thing is clear: Wembanyama looks noticeably different. And NBA fans have already started imagining what that could mean for the rest of the league.

The arms everyone is talking about

The biggest talking point isn't Wembanyama's height. It's his biceps. For years, critics pointed to the French star's slender frame as one of the few weaknesses in his game. Opposing teams often tried to counter his skill and length by attacking him physically in the paint. That strategy may become much harder this season.

Recent images have showcased a visibly stronger Wemby, with fans immediately noticing increased muscle definition in his arms and shoulders. Social media platforms were flooded with reactions comparing his current physique to previous seasons, with many concluding that the Spurs franchise cornerstone spent the offseason focused on adding strength.

For a player who already possesses elite shot-blocking instincts, perimeter skills, and unprecedented reach, additional strength could make him even more difficult to defend, and even more difficult to move.

The "French Alien" looks ready

The timing of the transformation has only fueled excitement. Wembanyama is coming off a season that ended in heartbreak after the Spurs fell to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals . While reaching the championship series represented a major milestone for San Antonio's rebuilding project, the loss left Wembanyama one step short of capturing the first NBA title of his career.

Fans have not forgotten. Judging by the reaction online, many believe the disappointment may have created an even more dangerous version of the player known as the "French Alien." Every new photo, highlight, or international performance has generated the same type of comments: Wembanyama looks stronger, taller, and motivated. And that's a frightening combination for the rest of the NBA.

The scary part isn't simply the physical transformation. It's what happens when that transformation is combined with Wembanyama's existing skill set. Even before this offseason, he was already one of basketball's most unique talents. Standing well over seven feet tall with guard-like ball handling, shooting ability, and defensive versatility, Wembanyama has consistently done things that should not be possible for someone his size.

He is widely regarded as one of the game's premier young stars and one of the most physically gifted players in NBA history. If he has truly added meaningful strength while maintaining his mobility and coordination, opposing defenses could face an even bigger challenge.

articles.title: LeBron James still can't forget Los Angeles as he celebrates major player's surprise return
articles.standfirst: The Lakers star was quick to react to Aaron Donald's comeback.
articles.summary: The Lakers star was quick to react to Aaron Donald's comeback.
articles.body:
LeBron James may have spent years building his own legacy in Los Angeles, but the Lakers superstar still clearly has plenty of affection for the city's other sporting icons.

That was obvious after Aaron Donald announced his stunning return to the Los Angeles Rams on a reported one-year, $20 million deal.

Donald celebrated the news on Instagram with a compilation of some of his best moments in a Rams uniform and a simple message.

James immediately joined the celebration.

"YESSIR!!!! LFG," James wrote with several speaking head emojis.

Aaron Donald's Rams return gets LeBron James excited

Donald retired in 2024 after 10 seasons with the Rams , ending what already looked like a complete Hall of Fame career.

He appeared in 154 regular season games, recording 543 tackles, 111 sacks and 176 tackles for loss while winning three Defensive Player of the Year awards and helping Los Angeles capture Super Bowl LVI.

Talk of a comeback intensified this summer after the Rams traded with the Cleveland Browns for five-time All-Pro pass rusher Myles Garrett in June.

Donald was then spotted training at the Rams ' facility last month, adding further fuel to speculation that he was preparing to return.

Donald knew about comeback for two weeks

Donald practiced with Los Angeles on Sunday for the first time in two years and admitted afterward that the decision had been taking shape for some time.

"To be honest with you, it was on and off for a while, but knew this decision about two weeks," Donald said. "I know the world was saying all types of things and nobody knew what was going on, but I kind of knew for two weeks."

He also revealed how closely he remained in contact with coach Sean McVay .

"But then I talked to Sean every single week, damn near every day, so we stayed in contact. I gave him all my updates, how I was feeling, how things were going so I know he got annoyed with answering all the questions in camp every day, so I felt bad for him at that point."

McVay hasn't yet confirmed whether Donald will be ready for the Rams ' Week 1 game against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia on September 10.

James , however, clearly doesn't need any more convincing. Donald is back in Los Angeles, and one of the city's biggest stars couldn't be happier about it.

articles.title: LeBron James gets news of ‘1-in-400-million’ bad luck incident that ruins teammate’s new house
articles.standfirst: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope’s Philadelphia arrival got off to an unbelievable start
articles.summary: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope’s Philadelphia arrival got off to an unbelievable start
articles.body:
T hey say there is no such thing as good or bad luck, just luck . But when you find out your new penthouse was struck by lightning and that the chances of an event like that happening were reportedly 1 in 400 million , you might start reconsidering that idea.

If LeBron James is superstitious, he might want to keep an eye on the luck of Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, his new teammate in Philadelphia . But if he prefers to look at the positive side, he can also take the bizarre incident as a sign that the Sixers’ luck could eventually work in their favor.

A nightmare welcome to Philadelphia

Caldwell-Pope’s new Philadelphia penthouse was struck by lightning just minutes after his wife, McKenzie, signed the lease , triggering a chaotic situation inside the building.

The strike caused flooding, disabled the elevators and forced the family to walk down 14 flights of stairs to safety. The couple’s movers had not yet finished bringing their belongings upstairs when they became trapped inside an elevator that was disabled by the lightning strike . Firefighters eventually had to rescue them.

Hours later, an electrician inspecting the damage gave the family an explanation that made the situation even more surreal: the unit had been struck by lightning in a way that reportedly had a 1-in-400-million chance of happening.

Caldwell-Pope’s new chapter could still bring better luck

The incident made for an unforgettable welcome to the city for Caldwell-Pope, who arrived in Philadelphia after agreeing to a buyout with the Memphis Grizzlies and signing a one-year, $3.8 million contract with the 76ers.

The move also reunites him with former Lakers teammate LeBron James, adding another familiar connection as Caldwell-Pope begins his new chapter in Philadelphia. ​ ​That unusual stroke of luck can also be looked at from another perspective. After all, the lightning strike already beat incredible odds . Now, according to various prediction markets, the Philadelphia 76ers’ chances of winning the NBA championship during the 2026-27 season currently sit between 10% and 13% across the major prediction markets.

As long as that probability is not a definitive zero , LeBron can trust that the math, luck and probability could eventually line up in their favor. The lightning strike already proved that something with a 1-in-400-million chance can happen, so nothing is absolutely impossible.

articles.title: Blake Griffin questions Lakers’ decision to give Bronny James $8 million guaranteed contract
articles.standfirst: The comments touch on one of the biggest debates surrounding LeBron James' oldest son
articles.summary: The comments touch on one of the biggest debates surrounding LeBron James' oldest son
articles.body:
Few players in recent NBA history have faced more scrutiny before playing their first professional game than Bronny James. The son of NBA legend LeBron James entered the league under a spotlight unlike any second-round pick before him, and now former NBA star Blake Griffin believes one decision by the Los Angeles Lakers made that spotlight even brighter.

Speaking candidly about Bronny's path to the NBA, Griffin said he had no issue with the Lakers selecting James with the 55th overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. Where he believes the organization made a mistake, however, was the contract that followed.

“If you can get drafted, go get drafted. I have zero issues with him getting drafted at the 55th pick. I have zero issues at the Lakers being like, ‘Yeah, we’re going to do this,’” Griffin said. “The thing that I think they probably messed up on is, don’t give him $8 million guaranteed. Give him what is normal for that pick.”

Griffin's argument isn't about the draft pick

The comments touch on one of the biggest debates surrounding Bronny's entry into the league. While many observers expected the Lakers to draft him in part to unite him with LeBron James , the fully guaranteed contract generated additional criticism because players selected late in the second round typically do not receive that level of financial commitment.

Griffin's remarks are notable because they are not a criticism of Bronny himself. The six-time NBA All-Star made it clear that he understands why James declared for the draft and why the Lakers chose to use the 55th pick on him. Bronny was selected by Los Angeles in the second round of the 2024 draft, creating the NBA's first father-son teammate pairing.

Instead, Griffin believes the guaranteed money became an unnecessary distraction.

“He made 10 times that in NIL. Maybe not 10 times, but he’s made his own money. And he also doesn’t ever have to worry about money,” Griffin added. “Just give him the normal thing, and you get everybody off his back. Have him play in the G League.”

In Blake's view, a more conventional second-round contract structure would have reduced accusations of favoritism and allowed Bronny to develop without constant discussion about his salary.

The reality of being LeBron's son

Whether fair or not, Bronny entered the NBA carrying expectations that most second-round selections never encounter. Ordinarily, the 55th pick in the draft receives little national attention. Most players chosen that late spend significant time in the G League , fighting for roster spots and proving they belong at the professional level.

Bronny's situation was different from the moment his name was called.

Every performance, every assignment to the G League, and every minute he played with the Lakers became national news. The guaranteed contract only intensified discussions about whether he had earned the opportunity or benefited from being the son of one of the greatest players in basketball history.

Griffin's comments suggest that the Lakers may have underestimated how much the contract itself would become part of the story. Of course, there is another side to the argument. The Lakers knew exactly what they were getting when they drafted Bronny.

Beyond his basketball potential, James represented a unique marketing opportunity and a historic moment for the franchise and the NBA. The organization helped create one of the league's most memorable milestones when LeBron and Bronny shared the court as teammates.

articles.title: Former NBA champion warns the Lakers about LeBron James and his departure
articles.standfirst: The Lakers have turned the page to Luka Doncic, but Horace Grant believes LeBron James’ departure leaves a massive void in Los Angeles.
articles.summary: The Lakers have turned the page to Luka Doncic, but Horace Grant believes LeBron James’ departure leaves a massive void in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers spent the summer ushering in the Luka Doncic era, but according to Horace Grant , that does not make LeBron James’ departure any less significant for the franchise.

The former Lakers player, who won the 2001 NBA championship with Los Angeles, warned that losing a player of James’ caliber will always create a major challenge, even when the organization has already identified its new franchise cornerstone.

“With a guy like LeBron, I don’t care if he’s 50 years old,” Grant told Action Network . “When he leaves a team, it can’t be good.”

Grant also praised James for maintaining an elite level of play despite his age.

“I have the highest praise for LeBron being 42 and still playing at a high level,” Grant said. “I’m a big fan of the young man.”

James’ departure represents one of the most significant transitions in recent Lakers history. The franchise is now built around Doncic, one of the NBA ’s most gifted offensive players, but it also means losing one of the most dominant figures the sport has ever seen.

Horace Grant believes Luka Doncic changed the Lakers’ future

Grant believes James quickly understood the direction the franchise was heading after Los Angeles acquired Doncic.

“I think LeBron knew that when Luka was traded there, that the writing was on the wall,” Grant said. “They were going to start building around him.”

That shift became official this summer when James informed the Lakers that he would play elsewhere during his 24th NBA season , ending an eight-year run in Los Angeles that included the 2020 championship and a long list of individual milestones.

The separation also reflected the priorities of both sides. The Lakers were looking to get younger, become more athletic and improve defensively around Doncić and Austin Reaves , while James pursued a new challenge at this stage of his career.

“Whenever LeBron leaves, it’s not a good thing,” Grant said, “but I think it was time for him to get re-energized.”

History shows replacing LeBron is not easy

Grant’s warning is supported by history. In James’ previous departures from Cleveland in 2010 , Miami in 2014 and Cleveland again in 2018 , each team failed to reach the playoffs the following season.

However, these Lakers have a different foundation. The franchise has Dončić as its new centerpiece, along with Austin Reaves and a roster specifically constructed to complement its young superstar.

Still, replacing LeBron’s impact will be a difficult task.

Last season, James averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists while continuing to show the ability to take over important playoff games at 41 years old .

His departure represents more than the loss of production. The Lakers are also losing his leadership, experience, playmaking ability and presence within the locker room.

Los Angeles has made it clear that the future belongs to Luka Doncic . Now the franchise must prove it can move into this new era without taking a step back from the success achieved during LeBron’s tenure.

The Luka era has officially begun. The first challenge will be proving the Lakers can move forward while replacing the impact of one of the greatest players in basketball history.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown sends chilling message ahead of first 76ers season: ‘I want blood this year’
articles.standfirst: The stellar guard wants to elevate his game and get another NBA championship soon
articles.summary: The stellar guard wants to elevate his game and get another NBA championship soon
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown is embracing his fresh start in Philadelphia with a mindset that should excite 76ers fans and concern the rest of the NBA. The five-time All-Star delivered one of the offseason's most striking quotes during a recent livestream, making it clear that he is entering his first season with the Philadelphia 76ers with a chip on his shoulder and something to prove.

“My mentality is kill,” Brown said. “I feel like I want blood this year. I feel like that’s the mentality.” As a player who spent the first decade of his career with the Boston Celtics , the comments reflect a competitor determined to make the most of a dramatic career change.

A new chapter after a blockbuster summer

Brown arrived in Philadelphia this summer in one of the NBA's biggest offseason moves. The former Celtics star joins a franchise that has transformed itself into a legitimate championship contender, pairing him with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and LeBron James on a roster loaded with star power.

The move marked the end of an era in Boston , where Brown developed into one of the league's premier two-way players and helped lead the Celtics to an NBA championship. But while many players might view a major trade as a chance to reset, Brown appears to be approaching it as fuel.

His comments suggest that the emotions of the past year, including Boston's stunning first-round playoff collapse against Philadelphia and the trade that followed, are still fresh in his mind. Now, he has an opportunity to channel that motivation into a new pursuit: bringing a title to the City of Brotherly Love.

Coming Off the Best Season of His Career

The timing of Brown's warning is especially noteworthy considering the level he reached last season. With Boston dealing with injuries and lineup changes, Brown carried a larger offensive burden than ever before. He responded by averaging a career-high 28.7 points per game while also contributing 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists.

Those numbers reinforced his status as one of the NBA's elite wings and helped make him one of the most coveted players in the league. Now entering his age-30 season, Brown appears convinced that his best basketball is still ahead of him.

The intensity behind Brown's comments is matched by the work he has already put in since arriving in Philadelphia. Although training camp is still weeks away, Brown revealed that he has spent much of the summer working out with his new teammates and getting acclimated to his new environment.

“We got some work to do ahead of us,” Jaylen said during the livestream. “I'm excited myself and working with the young guys... I've worked out with pretty much everybody on the team constantly. Talking, getting acclimated with one another. I think that's important.”

Expectations are sky high in Philadelphia

The 76ers have spent years searching for the right formula to maximize Embiid's championship window . This summer's aggressive roster construction signaled that the organization believes the time to win is now. Brown's arrival adds another proven scorer, defender and playoff performer to a team that already carried significant expectations.

That reality helps explain why his comments resonated so strongly. They were not the words of a player simply excited for a new opportunity. They sounded like the words of someone who feels personally motivated.

Whether that motivation stems from being traded, from Boston's disappointing finish, or from the challenge of proving he can thrive in a new situation, the result is the same: Brown is entering the season with an edge. Philadelphia's offseason has already made the 76ers one of the most talked-about teams in basketball.

Brown's latest comments will only add to the anticipation. At his introductory press conference earlier this month, Jaylen emphasized that winning is his primary focus and that nothing else truly motivates him at this stage of his career. His latest message took that mentality a step further.

articles.title: Stephen Curry puts contract extension with the Warriors on hold but delivers a very clear message about his future
articles.standfirst: Four-time champion in no rush over $136.7 million deal
articles.summary: Four-time champion in no rush over $136.7 million deal
articles.body:
Stephen Curry has reached the point in his career when every contract decision feels like it could define the final chapter. His latest message to the Golden State Warriors , however, made one thing sound far less complicated than the numbers.

The 38-year-old became eligible over the weekend for a two-year extension worth up to $136.7 million, a deal that could keep him under contract through the summer of 2029. Curry isn't rushing to sign it.

“There’s no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I’m pretty sure that’s going to happen,” Curry told NBC Sports Bay Area.

Curry is entering the final year of his current deal and is set to earn $62.6 million in 2026-27. Yet rather than allowing extension talks to become the story entering training camp, he wants the focus elsewhere.

“The deal and the contract stuff will happen at the right time, and we're not letting it be a distraction from our preparation for the season,” Curry said.

Warriors have bigger questions

Golden State ’s immediate concern isn't whether Curry wants to stay. It's whether the Warriors can build another meaningful playoff run around him.

The team missed the postseason again last year after falling to Phoenix in the play-in tournament, marking the second time in three seasons that Golden State failed to reach the playoffs.

Curry also missed a significant number of games, appearing only 41 times during an injury-disrupted campaign. That explains why his comments were as much about basketball as they were about money.

“Hopefully we’re healthy and we just have a chance to show what we’re capable of, myself included, after missing so many games last year,” Curry said.

The Warriors still believe their championship window has not completely closed, and Curry clearly shares that view.

More focused on Year 18 than next deal

“The goal stays the same,” Curry said. “Extension stuff, we’ll figure that out at the right time.

“But I’m ready for Year 18,” Curry added. “It’s kind of crazy that it’s been this long, and I’m still trying to play at a very high level to help us win, and I’ll be able to do my job.”

Curry made the remarks during the Workday Charity Classic in Palo Alto, which benefits Eat. Learn. Play., the foundation he runs with wife Ayesha .

Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy and executive vice president Kirk Lacob were also present. That made the setting fitting.

Curry doesn't sound like a player weighing his options or preparing for a dramatic departure.

He sounds like someone willing to let the contract take care of itself while he tries to extend the competitive life of the only NBA team he has ever known.

articles.title: Safaris and dreamlike landscapes: this was the extravagant honeymoon of the Knicks star
articles.standfirst: The couple celebrated their marriage with a trip to Africa, and Jordyn Woods shared images from an experience she described with a phrase impossible to ignore.
articles.summary: The couple celebrated their marriage with a trip to Africa, and Jordyn Woods shared images from an experience she described with a phrase impossible to ignore.
articles.body:
There are trips that are remembered for years and others that begin to be missed even before they come to an end. From what Jordyn Woods said, her honeymoon with Karl-Anthony Towns belongs, without a doubt, to the latter category.

After celebrating their marriage, the couple completely changed the pace of their lives to embark on a getaway that would be hard to forget. Africa was the chosen destination for a honeymoon filled with safaris, spectacular landscapes, and moments away from the world of the NBA and the exposure that normally surrounds the Knicks star.

“A dream I never wanted to wake up from”

Jordyn Woods was the one who decided to share part of the experience with her followers through a video on Instagram. The images showed some of the moments they experienced during the trip, but it was her words that ended up giving the post a special meaning.

“A dream that I didn’t know how to put into words, lived in nature with the love of my life,” wrote Jordyn. The phrase summed up a story they have both built over the years and that began long before they became husband and wife: first they were friends and, over time, that bond ended up turning into a relationship.

There was another phrase that explained even better what the trip meant for the model. “ Our honeymoon was like walking inside a dream I never wanted to wake up from” , she confessed alongside the images of the African adventure.

This trip was a pause after all the journey that led them to the altar. Between the preparations, the ceremony, and the attention that accompanied their marriage, Towns and Woods found the opportunity to disconnect and enjoy something much simpler: being together.

The contrast couldn't have been greater for Towns , either. Accustomed to the intensity of New York and the demands of being one of the Knicks ' stars, the player took advantage of the offseason to trade the arenas and lights of the NBA for the African wilderness.

Before long, it will be time to return to basketball and the routine of a new season. But before heading back to New York, Karl-Anthony Towns and Jordyn Woods gave themselves a memory that, judging by her words, neither of them seemed too eager to leave behind.

articles.title: What do Steph Curry and the Warriors need to do in order to compete for another championship?
articles.standfirst: Golden State has gone from championship standard-bearers to a franchise searching for answers
articles.summary: Golden State has gone from championship standard-bearers to a franchise searching for answers
articles.body:
The question hanging over the Golden State Warriors is whether the NBA franchise can still build a contender around Steph Curry or not. That reality became even more apparent after the iconic player became eligible over the weekend for a two-year contract extension worth up to $136.7 million, a deal that could keep the future Hall of Famer under contract through the summer of 2029. Yet the 38-year-old superstar is not rushing to put pen to paper.

On the surface, that might sound like a negotiating tactic. In reality, it appears to be something far more important. Curry wants to see a path forward. After all, Golden State missed the playoffs for the second time in three seasons after losing to the Phoenix Suns in the play-in tournament. The Warriors have gone from championship standard-bearers to a franchise searching for answers, and time is becoming the most valuable commodity they have.

The four-time NBA champion appeared in just 41 games last season because of injuries, a reminder that even the greatest shooters in basketball history are not immune to age. Curry remains elite when healthy, but the organization can no longer operate under the assumption that it has unlimited opportunities left to chase another title.

So what exactly do the Warriors need to do?

No, the Warriors should not trade Curry. In fact, trading him would solve almost none of the franchise's problems. Even if Golden State received a massive haul of draft picks and young players, the move would effectively signal the end of the most successful era in franchise history. Curry is not just the face of the organization; he remains its best player.

When healthy, he is still capable of carrying an offense, drawing defensive attention few players in NBA history have commanded, and changing playoff series with his shooting. More importantly, Curry has earned the right to determine how this chapter ends. Unless he specifically requests a trade, Golden State should continue building around him.

The issue isn't that Curry can no longer be the centerpiece of a contender. The issue is that the supporting cast has not been good enough. The Warriors need another star, and this is where the conversation becomes difficult.

Warriors' championship teams always had more than Curry

There was Klay Thompson in his prime. There was Draymond Green anchoring the defense. There was Kevin Durant during two title runs. There was Andrew Wiggins playing the best basketball of his career during the 2022 championship season. The current roster lacks that caliber of second star.

The Warriors have talented players, but they do not have another consistent All-NBA-level performer capable of easing the burden on Curry. That should be the front office's top priority. Whether through a trade or a major free-agent acquisition, Golden State needs another player who can create offense, score efficiently, and carry the team when Curry sits or misses games.

The problem is that such players rarely become available, and the Warriors no longer possess the treasure chest of assets they once had. Still, standing still is not an option. One of the most glaring issues for Golden State over the last few seasons has been athleticism.

The Warriors' dynasty teams were built on skill and intelligence, but they also had youth, energy, and defensive versatility. Today's roster often looks older and slower than many of the Western Conference contenders. The Oklahoma City Thunder, San Antonio Spurs, Houston Rockets, and Minnesota Timberwolves all feature younger cores with superior athleticism.

Golden State cannot turn back the clock, but it can prioritize acquiring players who bring speed, length, and defensive flexibility. That does not necessarily mean a complete roster overhaul. It does mean that every personnel decision should be made with an eye toward becoming more dynamic on both ends of the floor.

articles.title: Russell Westbrook was traded for Chris Paul in the NBA and now they’re trading alley-oops aboard a yacht
articles.standfirst: Seven years after the blockbuster deal that linked their careers, the retired point guards are celebrating 39 combined NBA seasons with their families and friends
articles.summary: Seven years after the blockbuster deal that linked their careers, the retired point guards are celebrating 39 combined NBA seasons with their families and friends
articles.body:
The ball rises above the deck and Russell Westbrook goes after it. Moments later, the roles are reversed and Chris Paul gets his opportunity to finish. For 39 combined NBA seasons, plays like these came with defenders, packed arenas and something important on the scoreboard. This time, the basket is attached to a yacht and the only thing waiting beneath them is the water.

Westbrook and Paul have been enjoying a vacation reportedly off the Italian coast with their wives, Nina Westbrook and Jada Paul, as well as family members and friends. Paul shared footage of the alley-oops with the simple caption “Retirement…,” while Westbrook posted another angle to his Instagram Story accompanied by Forrest Frank’s song “HAPPY.” The NBA soon reposted the moment. The basketball remained, but everything that once made it feel like work had disappeared.

In July 2019, Westbrook and Paul became the centerpieces of one of the biggest trades of their generation. Houston sent Paul, first-round selections in 2024 and 2026 and the rights to two additional pick swaps to Oklahoma City in exchange for Westbrook.

The Rockets reunited Westbrook with former Thunder teammate James Harden, while Paul landed on a franchise many expected to begin rebuilding after Westbrook’s departure ended an 11-year era.

Now Westbrook and Paul are passing the ball just for fun

Their stories did not unfold as anyone expected. Westbrook spent only one season in Houston before beginning a journey that took him through Washington, Los Angeles, Denver and Sacramento. Paul responded to doubts about his future by leading a young Thunder team to the playoffs, then helped Phoenix reach the 2021 NBA Finals. The transaction separated their paths, but it also connected their names forever.

Paul retired in February after 21 seasons as a 12-time All-Star and the second-leading player in NBA history in both assists and steals. Westbrook followed on August 12 after 18 seasons, leaving as a nine-time All-Star, the 2017 MVP and the league’s career leader with 209 triple-doubles.

Together, they produced 39 seasons, 21 All-Star selections and two careers destined to be remembered among the greatest point guards the game has seen.

Neither finished with an NBA championship. Westbrook reached the Finals with Oklahoma City in 2012, and Paul made it there with Phoenix nine years later. But aboard the yacht, there were no questions about missing rings, no trade rumors and no debate about what either man still needed to prove.

They were simply two friends taking turns passing the ball, attacking the rim and laughing with the people who had supported them through the longest years of their careers.

Seven years ago, Westbrook and Paul were exchanged as enormously valuable pieces of an NBA business deal. Now they are on the same boat by choice, setting each other up for alley-oops with no pressure and no result to worry about.

articles.title: LeBron James sends fierce message of support as Bronny faces ongoing Lakers pressure
articles.standfirst: The NBA icon made clear his sons will never face their struggles alone.
articles.summary: The NBA icon made clear his sons will never face their struggles alone.
articles.body:
LeBron James has sent a powerful message to his sons at a time when Bronny James is facing increasing pressure to prove himself with the Los Angeles Lakers .

The four-time NBA champion shared a quote on Instagram that underlined exactly where he stands as a father, regardless of what happens on the basketball court.

"To my son... Never hesitate to come to me and say, 'Dad, I'm not okay.' Even on my hardest days, I will always show up for you. Every time. No hesitation. I'm your father. And I'll love you for the rest of my life," James shared.

The message applies to both Bronny and his younger brother Bryce , but its timing is particularly significant given the uncertainty surrounding Bronny's future in Los Angeles.

Bronny James faces a crucial Lakers test

Bronny's journey has already been far from straightforward.

He suffered cardiac arrest in July 2023 before eventually returning to basketball and reaching the NBA, but the Lakers now have to determine what role he can realistically earn.

Tyler Watts of Lake Show Life believes the next stage is entirely in Bronny's hands.

"Bronny has an opportunity. That is all fans ask for after his first two years. Now it is on the guard to adapt, or it will be time for the purple and gold to move on," Watts wrote.

Coach JJ Redick has previously identified defensive pressure, attacking downhill and disrupting opposing guards as areas where Bronny can make an impact.

The challenge is producing those qualities consistently.

LeBron can protect Bronny off the court

Bronny's positional fit remains another concern.

Watts described him as a "player without a position," with questions over whether he has enough size to thrive as a shooting guard or enough playmaking to operate regularly at point guard.

That leaves Bronny needing to prove he can defend, shoot and contribute enough offensively to earn meaningful minutes.

LeBron can't make those basketball decisions for him.

What he can do is ensure his son knows that criticism, uncertainty and the pressure attached to the James name won't have to be handled alone.

"Every time. No hesitation," James ' message said.

The Lakers may eventually have to make a difficult decision about Bronny's future, but there is considerably less uncertainty about where his father will stand.

articles.title: A new era for the James family as LeBron and Savannah share proud Zhuri moment
articles.standfirst: Their youngest child has officially started a major new chapter.
articles.summary: Their youngest child has officially started a major new chapter.
articles.body:
LeBron James and Savannah James are watching their family enter another new era, and this time the milestone has nothing to do with professional basketball.

Their 11-year-old daughter, Zhuri Nova James , officially started sixth grade this week, beginning middle school as her proud parents marked the emotional occasion on social media.

With Bronny James now building his own NBA career and Bryce James playing college basketball at Arizona, Zhuri remains the youngest of LeBron and Savannah's three children .

Savannah admitted that seeing her daughter take another big step toward growing up wasn't easy.

"The girl started 6th grade today... Am I okay? Not really. Did I cry about it? Yes. Am I so proud of her and excited to see her continue to grow into an amazing young woman? Absolutely. Go be great Baby!!" Savannah wrote.

LeBron James sends emotional message to Zhuri

LeBron reshared his wife's message before posting one of his own for the daughter he affectionately calls "mama face."

"My Baby Z first day of 6th grade today! Man o Man!! Ammo is fully loaded and I ain't playing about my Princess LOL," James wrote.

He then offered Zhuri some advice for the school year ahead.

"Have a wonderful school year mama face, have fun and continue to be YOU! It's always ENOUGH! Love you."

The morning wasn't entirely emotional.

LeBron also shared footage from their journey to school, including a moment when Zhuri surprised him by knowing the words to "Phone Tap" by AZ featuring Nature and Dr. Dre.

"She really knew the song though! I was like WHAT! lol," James wrote.

James family enters another new chapter

The milestone comes as all three James children increasingly begin following their own paths.

Bronny is entering his third NBA season with the Los Angeles Lakers , while Bryce is continuing his basketball career with the Arizona Wildcats .

Zhuri's first day of middle school offered LeBron and Savannah a very different proud parent moment.

Basketball has defined much of the public story surrounding the James family, but Savannah's emotional admission made clear that watching their youngest child grow up can mean just as much.

"Go be great Baby!!" she wrote.

For LeBron and Savannah , another chapter in their children's lives has officially begun.

articles.title: Clippers owner Steve Ballmer suspended one year as NBA reveals what he did for Kawhi Leonard
articles.standfirst: The NBA said Ballmer knowingly helped Leonard obtain off-court income
articles.summary: The NBA said Ballmer knowingly helped Leonard obtain off-court income
articles.body:
Steve Ballmer has never behaved like a distant owner. He sits near the court, jumps from his seat, pumps his fists and celebrates Clippers baskets with the emotion of a lifelong fan. He built Intuit Dome to give the franchise a home of its own. Now, the NBA has ordered the most visible man in the building to step away from all league and team activities for an entire year.

The league announced the punishment Wednesday after an independent investigation found that Ballmer knowingly sought to help Kawhi Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities.

According to the NBA’s findings, Ballmer also approved a business agreement that he knew was necessary for Aspiration to enter into an endorsement deal with Leonard and failed to establish conditions that ensured the Clippers followed salary-cap circumvention rules.

The consequences will remain long after Ballmer returns

Ballmer’s suspension is only part of a historic punishment. The Clippers were fined $30 million and must surrender one first-round Draft pick in each year from 2029 through 2033. Business operations president Gillian Zucker was suspended without pay for one year, while basketball operations president Lawrence Frank received a six-month suspension.

The organization will also operate under an NBA compliance and monitoring program for five years.

Leonard was ordered to pay the league $700,000, while his former business manager, Dennis Robertson, was banned from conducting business with NBA teams for five years. The investigation concluded that the Clippers initiated and facilitated endorsement opportunities for Leonard with Aspiration, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics and Lockton Insurance, all companies that conducted business with the franchise.

The most controversial arrangement was Leonard’s reported four-year, $28 million endorsement deal with the now-bankrupt Aspiration. Leonard was accused of performing little or no visible work under the agreement.

He said after the ruling that he entered the deals in good faith and did not know about any attempt to circumvent the salary cap. The Clippers and Ballmer had also denied wrongdoing when the allegations first surfaced.

NBA Commissioner Adam Silver described the case as involving “flagrant violations” and serious leadership failures. The announced penalties are final and binding under an agreement between the NBA and the players’ union, although investigators continue to receive information and the league has left open the possibility of further action.

Ballmer will eventually return, but the cost of the decisions made during the Kawhi Leonard era will follow the Clippers through at least 2033.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard’s ‘no-show’ deal puts Clippers’ $100 million screen maker under federal scrutiny
articles.standfirst: The company behind the enormous Halo Board was supposed to help fans see everything. Now regulators are asking about the one thing nobody could see
articles.summary: The company behind the enormous Halo Board was supposed to help fans see everything. Now regulators are asking about the one thing nobody could see
articles.body:
I nside the Clippers’ Intuit Dome , almost nothing is supposed to escape the audience’s eyes. The $100 million Halo Board surrounds the court with more than 233 million LEDs and enough digital space to equal 3,592 60-inch televisions. It was designed so fans could watch every basket, expression and replay from almost anywhere in the arena. Yet the company that built it is now facing questions about something nobody remembers seeing: Kawhi Leonard doing any work for a multimillion-dollar sponsorship.

That question moved beyond basketball Wednesday. During a Daktronics earnings call, acting chief financial officer Howard Atkins disclosed that the NBA had requested information from the company and that the Securities and Exchange Commission was also seeking information concerning Daktronics and Leonard. Atkins said the company was cooperating but would not comment further.

The SEC has not revealed exactly what it is examining, and requesting information does not by itself establish that Daktronics or Leonard violated federal law.

The company built something enormous but allegedly received nothing visible from Kawhi

According to reporting from Pablo Torre Finds Out, Leonard had an undisclosed multimillion-dollar sponsorship agreement with Daktronics , which built the Halo Board as part of the company’s largest single-year order volume in history.

Investigators found no public advertising campaign, promotional appearance or other visible work performed by Leonard . That absence was especially unusual because Daktronics primarily sells scoreboards and display systems to teams, airports and other businesses not products to ordinary fans and former employees said celebrity endorsements were not part of its traditional marketing strategy.

The most revealing details may be found in a series of internal emails obtained by Torre. Beginning in March 2021, Clippers marketing employees repeatedly asked Daktronics representatives whether they had met with Leonard and his uncle and then-business representative, Dennis Robertson. They asked about promotional “activations,” tried to secure a date and later followed up about autographs.

The emails do not prove that improper payments were made , but they reveal something remarkably human beneath all the corporate language: people behind the scenes appeared to be struggling to get Leonard to do something anything that could be shown as evidence of a real sponsorship.

The NBA has now concluded that the Clippers improperly facilitated outside income opportunities involving Leonard and four companies that did business with the team: Aspiration, Daktronics, Boingo Wireless and Lockton Insurance. The league stripped Los Angeles of five first-round picks from 2029 through 2033, fined the franchise $30 million and suspended owner Steve Ballmer for one year.

Leonard was fined $700,000 but not suspended. In a statement through his agent, Leonard said he entered the agreements in good faith and had no knowledge of an attempt to circumvent the salary cap, although he accepted responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within his inner circle.

The NBA can take away draft picks, issue fines and suspend executives . The SEC’s investigation could introduce an entirely different kind of accountability, although its scope and potential consequences remain unknown.

For Daktronics, the alleged sponsorship has now produced the one thing it apparently lacked when Leonard was under contract: enormous public visibility. The Halo Board can replay almost any moment from every possible angle, but the question hanging over its maker remains painfully simple : What exactly was Kawhi being paid to do?

articles.title: Klay Thompson indirectly poses a challenge to Stephen Curry for the new NBA season
articles.standfirst: Thompson is now a member of the Miami Heat and wants to make history at his new franchise.
articles.summary: Thompson is now a member of the Miami Heat and wants to make history at his new franchise.
articles.body:
When it comes to having an exciting offseason, Miami Heat and Golden State Warriors fans had very opposite experiences this summer. While the Warriors are practically running it back with the same roster around Stephen Curry , the Heat welcomed Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson to South Florida.

The vibes are certainly different in respective locker rooms, although it's yet to be seen if Miami's additions actually lead to more wins. As of right now, both Giannis and Thompson appear very happy with their new surroundings . Thompson, in particular, appears eager to make history - and may have challenged Curry , his former teammate.

Klay Thompson wants to break Duncan Robinson's Miami Heat three-point record

A new video surfaced this week of Thompson getting acclimated to his Miami environment. While in the Heat locker room, Thompson revealed his goal for the upcoming season: Breaking the Heat's single-season three-point record .

To answer Thompson's question, the record was set by Duncan Robinson during the 2019-20 season, when he sunk 270 three-pointers . Thompson has surpassed that number on two previous occasions, both with the Warriors: 301 three-pointers in 2022-23 and 276 three-pointers in 2015-16 .

Curry, as the literal all-time leader in three-pointers made, has surpassed that 270 number on 10 occasions . He had done that in five straight seasons before an injury-shortened 2025-26 campaign. Perhaps Thompson's goal can prove to be a motivating factor for Curry in a friendly competition of sorts.

articles.title: LeBron James rides one of a kind new bike that was made just for him
articles.standfirst: LeBron James is adding another sport to his offseason routine
articles.summary: LeBron James is adding another sport to his offseason routine
articles.body:
LeBron James is going through multiple new beginnings this offseason. Even as an established legend, the 41-year-old continues to add new experiences to his list while growing his image as an iconic sports figure, and he clearly has no plans to stop.

When retirement eventually arrives, there will be plenty to keep James busy. Now, he is adding another sport to his roster . It is no longer just about basketball or golf, as cycling is also becoming part of his world.

James is now collaborating with Canyon, and the brand revealed a one-of-a-kind gravel bike built specifically for him, as he is also one of the company’s shareholders . The custom 32-inch-wheeled Grizl CF was engineered from the ground up for the 6-foot-9 NBA superstar, whose size falls outside the dimensions most production bike frames are designed to accommodate.

The larger 32-inch wheels are designed to roll over rocks, ruts and rough terrain with less rolling resistance while reducing the impact on the rider. Canyon also added extra support to handle James’ size and the demands he would put on the bike . It also features custom-made thru-axles and a custom seat clamp.

Every detail was designed for him

Everything Canyon did was specifically tailored to James, as explained by Wolfgang Kohl, the company’s lead engineer. The bike was not simply made by enlarging an existing frame. Its geometry, structure and load requirements had to be re-engineered because the forces placed on the bike do not scale in the same way as its dimensions.

That meant the entire system had to be redesigned to make sure t he bike could properly respond to its rider and function as intended.

Cycling is not new to LeBron

Some may think cycling has only now entered LeBron’s life through this new collaboration, but the sport has been part of his life since he was young. James has a long history with cycling dating back to his childhood in Akron, Ohio.

He used to ride his bike to basketball practice, visit friends and travel around his hometown. His connection to the sport has also continued into his business ventures, with his LRMR Ventures group taking an equity stake in Canyon in 2022.

articles.body:
Steph Curry wants to keep his own narrative under control. A lot has been said about what his path should look like as he considers his future in the NBA, but everything points to him being clear about his goals. Continuing his career with the Warriors appears to be one of them, along with being sharp and precise as he enters his 18th NBA season.

The power remains in his hands and his shooting. Everyone knows the Warriors revolve around Curry, and he wants to represent the franchise the right way in what could be his final year with the team. The Warriors want Curry, and Curry has long maintained that he wants to wear only one jersey throughout his NBA career. Based on his latest workout, it all comes down to consistency.

The video he recently posted on TikTok was a double-edged sword. Curry is trying to ease Warriors fans' frustration after the team failed to make the playoffs last season by showing patience and confidence. His wife, Ayesha Curry, recently said that good things are coming, and with her husband being the hardest worker she knows, there is reason to expect those things to be good.

His commitment to Golden State remains as strong as ever

The clearest sign that Curry trusts the franchise as much as he trusts himself is the fact that the Warriors want him, while Curry has long maintained that he wants to wear only one jersey throughout his NBA career.

For now, the only thing that can be assured is that Curry is ready and willing to enter the NBA season recharged and more precise than ever. Thousands of things can be said about his future, but he is focused on doing what is in front of him at this stage of his career.
